# SPE Round 5 plan: invoice extraction

"Go again" means I run round 5 using the round 4 evidence. I record each choice as a default that you can override next round. I commit locally after each step and never push.

## 0. Inputs I read before planning

- `spe/prediction-log.md`, round 4. Q measured 0.93 against a prediction of 0.91, which was a hit. R measured 0.88 against a prediction of 0.95, which was a miss. The naive "same as last round" guess (0.90) was closer for R than my prediction was.
- The Why that broke was "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals." That Why assumed cleanup only helps. The cleanup tool also drops line items on two-column layouts.
- `spe/failures.md` F9: "OCR cleanup drops two-column line items (agent, r04). Fix: open."
- The "Proposed for round 5" table (P1 to P3) and the draft prediction that the round 4 learn step left behind.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the proposals

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1. Keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopt as new config S | It targets F9 directly. S differs from R in one thing only, which is the layout gate. |
| P2. Add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Reject for r05 (default) | No reference fields exist for these invoices, and only the AP lead can supply them. Adding them now would also change the eval set, so the r05 results could not be compared with r04. I log this as an open decision. |
| P3. Drop config P | Adopt (default) | P trails Q on every metric. Dropping it saves 60 trials. P's earlier numbers stay in the log as history. |

### Requirement table for round 5

New IDs continue from the last ID in `spe/spec/spec.md`. Below I write them as R5-a to R5-f, and I will renumber them to the next free IDs when I write the file.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-a | Config S equals R, except that the OCR cleanup wrapper returns the raw OCR text unchanged when a page has two text columns. The prompt, the model, and the other tools stay the same as in R. | P1, r04 F9 | A config diff check confirms that the only difference between R and S is the gate |
| R5-b | On two-column invoices, S extracts the same number of line items as the reference. | r04 F9 | Code check `line_item_count_match` on the two-column subset |
| R5-c | Every one of the 60 invoices carries a hand-made layout tag (`one_column` or `two_column`). The tags are stored with the reference data, and trials never see them. | r04 F9 | Grader selftest confirms that all 60 invoices are tagged |

| R5-f | Config P is retired. Its spec rows stay in the file with the note "retired r05, trails Q on every metric." | P3 | No run. The note is reviewed in the commit diff. |

Naive guess for comparison: every config stays at its r04 number, and S takes R's r04 number (0.88).

## 3. Evaluate

### Harness: `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`

- `ROUND = 5` is set in one constant. Every file name and prompt is built from it.
- Configs: `["Q", "R", "S"]`. The eval set is the same 60 invoices with the AP lead's reference fields, plus the new layout tags.
- Trials return a fixed JSON schema: vendor, invoice_number, date, line_items[], total, po_mismatch[], and gate_decision (S only).
- All graders are code checks. This round does not need a judge.
- Trials run in a directory that contains no references, layout tags, graders, or predictions. After the run, I scan each transcript for reads of those paths and void any trial that touched them.

### Gates before launch

1. Grader selftest. The oracle answers pass. Empty and wrong answers fail. All 60 invoices have a layout tag.
2. Control. I regrade the round 4 transcripts with the r05 graders. Q must come back at 0.93 and R at 0.88 on field accuracy. If either differs, I halt and treat the difference as a grader failure.
3. Dry run on 3 cells: S on a two-column invoice, S on a scanned single-column invoice, and Q on any invoice.

### Workflow arguments

- `round: 5`, `configs: ["Q","R","S"]`, `invoices: 60`, `trials_per_cell: 1`
- `split_cell_extra_trials: 2` on up to 20 invoices where configs disagree
- `trial_cap: 250`, `token_cap: 7000000`. A trial that would cross a cap is skipped, and the skip is logged.
- Final steps: failure analysis, then a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The base run is 180 trials (60 invoices × 3 configs). Split-cell reruns add up to 40 more, for a maximum of 220. At about 25k tokens per trial, that is about 5.5M tokens. Dropping P saves about 1.5M tokens compared with running four configs.

### Halt conditions

I halt and report if the run hits a cap, a trial reads the answer key, the control regrade does not reproduce r04, or the run surfaces a decision only you can make.

## 4. Order of work after approval

1. Save the pasted text and "go again" word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Write the round 5 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and the rows above to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r05 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` and the author line "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode". Commit `SPE r05 predict: S gates OCR cleanup on two-column layouts`.
3. Build the gate, the layout tags, the new checks, and the harness. Run the three gates. Commit `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When it finishes, commit `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out after the completion notice arrives. That means the prediction log with "Which Why broke", new F-numbers, and an update to F9's Fix line, a "Proposed for round 6" table, `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml`, and the README. Commit `SPE r05 learn` and tag `spe-r05`.

Stop rule status: the predictions have not matched the results for 3 rounds in a row, because round 4 had a miss. The loop continues after round 5.
